title: Sunday matinee dances and head arrangements at the Saratoga
summary: The empty club filled for Sunday matinees; the band hardly rehearsed and played mostly head arrangements with Red Allen fitting in.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: But the numbers you were recording at this time are some of the hottest numbers in Jazz, and they were well-

Oh, we played. We played down there. Every Sunday they would have a matinee dance. The place would be packed and jammed. Every Sunday afternoon. The rest of the week, there'd be nobody in the place. But that matinee, that's why it was packed and jammed. That band was working. Believe me. And we enjoyed working. Because it was a younger bunch of people, you know. And we just enjoyed. We wouldn't miss a matinee for nothin'. We'd miss any other night of the week, but we wouldn't miss a matinee.
But you must have rehearsed for this during the week.

We didn't rehearse much. We was rehearsin' on the job, one of them things, you know. We got a kick out of playing, and we'd get together: 'We'll do so-and-so-and-so, and we'll do this and that and the other.' Most of them was head arrangements. Most of them were really head arrangements. But we'd get a kick out of playing them and doing them.
Yeah, when Red come in that band, he just fell right in. Had a different band all the time. But it was a good band. I listen to some of them tapes and things, you know,
some of that old stuff. You know what ones I've been listenin' to lately? The ones on Wilton Crawley(?). I said, 'Man, he's not too bad for what he was doing.'
